policy.evidence: Paired constraint predictions made before each new optimizer observation; the research data fit both models but do not count as prior-adoption trials

evaluation.rule: Public evaluation coordinates and all final Program/GP predictions are frozen after each optimizer run. After every selected run is complete, a separate actual simulator stream supplies shared measurements and evaluator-only true constraint means. Evaluation calls never enter the controller and are reported separately.
evaluation.additional_requested_metrics: Record which experimental controls provide useful measured objective values, objective prediction errors on actual future observations, final objective-GP predictions on the same frozen independent controls when available, and the best measured point after the mechanism change. Preserve the original constraint Program/GP errors, confirmation and revision sequence, feasibility, and paid costs.

protocol.method: After a frozen objective candidate has been rejected and a future paid control remains, retain its hypothesis and original negative evidence for renewed predictive comparison. If at least four future labels remain, first try adding the already supported constraint program as a learned objective coordinate; accept this representation proposal only when grouped cross-validation improves both identifiable base representations and the constant reference. Fit only then on already paid labels and begin a new future comparison. Without a supported repair, resume the original candidate only when its paired-evidence upper margin still crosses zero. Share forecasts on later ordinary paid controls and actively scan the public control pool for the greatest noise-normalized feasible untested disagreement. Objective head installation still requires the original future-support rule. Rejecting at the final observation cannot change the installed objective or final recommendation. Helper fitting, scanning and forecast work are included in objective_research.compute_cost; report that controller work separately from native KG timing.
protocol.selection: All10 old paths with rejected frozen objective candidates and later real observations. Two of517 reject only at stage64; rerun one as a last-observation control and reuse the other. Four additional no-entry controls complete the fifteen-case development roster. This covers both diagnosed useful candidates, zero-noise stable tasks, strongly unfavorable candidates, and a rejection with only one remaining observation.
protocol.reuse_rule: The new predictive and experimental branch requires an already rejected frozen candidate before a later paid control. Reuse502 old paths without that entry, excluding five executed controls. Original shared-observation entry is included because all10 paths retain paid observations after rejection regardless of the later action purpose. Reused records remain previously executed v0.51 evidence, not new v0.52 trajectories.
protocol.accounting: Ten historical new-method runs plusfive controls and54 fresh paired runs cost2208 online calls. Fresh shared acquisition costs384 initial and1920 evaluator calls. Each arm uses32 initial and32 online calls. Development15 costs480 online calls and is included once; there are no further unexecuted affected historical cases after development. Reuse all old initialization, evaluator and baseline outcomes. Report added comparisons, predictions and native KG work separately; no new older-method, vanilla or CodeAgent runs.
protocol.source_loading: Freeze the current cleaned live v0.51 eleven modules directly, rather than restore the earlier passive experiment's unreachable nomination branches. Freeze the complete new intervention module package, including objective_reentry.py and decision_experiments.py, before development and all fresh acquisition.
protocol.limitations: The existing517 are development evidence, including the newly inspected prior27. The predeclared fresh27 remain separate and run only after development is promising. The two diagnosed candidates are accurate on existing evaluator controls but their observed local comparison failures remain real. Missing historical measured objective evaluator labels remain missing, and historical timing does not establish simultaneous runtime improvement.
